svg.text: First half — how much: one fitted equation, one constraint, and every axis added since
Second half — which tokens: compute decides how many; a pipeline decides which — and someone decides the pipeline
Common Crawl → extraction → language ID → quality filter → deduplication → decontamination → PII → mixing and order
each stage has a failure mode; W1's verbatim n = 8 sample, W2's Traditional Chinese gap and MMLU all land on this line

g.text: the three questions in order: how much (derive it) → what else costs (add an axis) → can a fit be trusted (methodology) →
which tokens (the plant) → how to mix and order them → what to do when the good water runs out (synthesis, collapse)
one sentence for today: a scaling law is a fit, not a measurement —
and 2026's models are not breaking Chinchilla; they are optimising a different bill
